round2_ask_classifications.ask1_argv_table_note: DISCHARGED — and the audit-class argument VERIFIED as correct, not just plausible. I re-derived it against the code: (a) the -m-value safety claim is mechanically accurate — gitutil.MaterializeStageCommit builds argv as [commit-tree, (-S,) tree, -p, parent, -m, msg] via exec.Command (discrete argv, no shell), so the subject reaches git solely as the -m flag's option-argument, which git consumes unconditionally as a literal and never re-scans for option-likeness; RejectOptionLike exists to guard POSITIONAL ref/tree operands against exactly the re-scan risk the -m slot never carries, which is the same standing justification CommitTreeMerge's message operand already has in this table. (b) The class (opClassRejectOptionLikeGated) is rightly unchanged: it names the gating applied to tree and parent — the two operands that need it and still get it at the top of the function — and subject is prose, neither a ref/tree operand nor an id-render position, so no other class in the table's taxonomy fits better. (c) The note now also carries the real residual-risk story I asked for: operator text forging a Mindspec-Stage line is defeated by ReadStageTrailer's duplicate-trailer-is-ambiguous rule (G2), failing safe to foreign-clear + full re-gate — I traced that path in round 2 and it still holds. The count-exact ratchet stays green (lint suite ok).
